collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Travelers bring back seeds descended from the village's own lost beans: plant them all now, or trade some first.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A traveler has come back from a far island with a bag of speckled beans: the same beans Isola grew long ago, lost in a blight. (subject) wants to plant every one of them at once. (friend) wants to share some at the great seed exchange first, so the beans grow in many gardens in case one fails. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) plants them all in the best garden. They grow beautifully. Then the pigs get in. (friend) has secretly saved a handful. They start again, and this time share them around.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The beans go to twenty gardens. Some fail. Most grow. Within two years, the speckled beans are back in every family's pot, and the old bean song is sung again at harvest.
